summary: The root وأل (wAl) refers to a "jawaliqun" or "jiwaliqun," which is a large sack or pannier. For a more detailed understanding, one should consult the entry for the root جلق (jlq).
lane: جُوَالِقٌ جوالق and جُوَالَقٌ and جِوَالِقٌ : see art. جلق .

provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: : see آلَ, in art. اول, in two places.

First, and former; preceding all others, and preceding another. See art. أول أَوَائِلُ السُّوَرِ The first parts, or beginnings, of the chapters of the Kur-án. جَآءَ فِى أَوَائِلِ القَوْمِ He came among the first comers of the people. (Msb.) And الأَوَائِلُ The people of former ages; as also الأَوَّلُونَ. لَقِيتُهُ عَامًا أَوَّلَ means I met him [ in a former year. ] before this year, though by several years. (Alee El-Kári, in his Expos.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
